target.title: fix(ssh-tunnel): handle spawn error to prevent unhandled rejection crash
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/usr/bin/ssh` is missing from the system (ENOENT), `spawn()` emits an async `error` event on the child process. Without an `error` listener, Node.js crashes the entire process with an unhandled error event. The tunnel setup code only listens for `exit`, so the `Promise.race` hangs until timeout instead of rejecting cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds `child.once("error", reject)` in the same Promise constructor that already watches for `exit`, forwarding the spawn error into the standard rejection path used by `Promise.race`.

## User Impact

SSH tunnel setup now rejects with a descriptive ENOENT error instead of crashing the gateway when `/usr/bin/ssh` is absent.

## Evidence

**Regression test** ("rejects with the spawn error when ssh binary is missing"):

The mock spawn emits an error asynchronously via `queueMicrotask(() => child.emit("error", spawnError))`, matching real Node.js spawn behavior. The test verifies the Promise rejects with "ENOENT" rather than the process crashing.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Before**: spawn error event → no handler → unhandled error → process crash
**After**: `child.once("error", reject)` → Promise rejects → caller receives "ENOENT"

## Risk

Low. One-line addition in an existing Promise constructor. The `error` handler runs alongside the existing `exit` handler; neither affects the happy path.
